fr.recommendations:
• Mark all access points with visible address numbers or building identifiers so responders can quickly confirm correct entry points.

• Mark the rear access route with reflective signage indicating limited access and any turn-around restrictions.

• Keep the dumpster enclosure clear of overflow materials that could block movement along adjacent drive aisles.

• Post a site map near the primary access point showing the locations of both structures, all drive aisles, and the access road.

• Mark the detached building with its own visible address or unit identifier on the side facing the nearest drive aisle.

• Keep internal drive aisles clear of parked vehicles and stored materials to allow emergency vehicles to move between the main building and the detached building.

• Identify a designated staging area in the open area and mark it so responders can use it without coordinating on arrival.

wildfire.conditions: Vegetated Perimeter; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations: Enhancing defensible space around the property by increasing the separation between vegetated areas and the structure could prove beneficial. Consider managing and reducing vegetation directly adjacent to the structure to minimize potential structure exposure. Preserving the open terrain could provide a valuable buffer and reduce continuity of fuels, potentially limiting fire spread towards the building. Furthermore, regular maintenance of vegetated perimeters, including trimming or removal of denser clusters, might support suppression efforts while contributing to long-term wildfire resilience. Proactively managing these aspects would also be advantageous for maintaining accessibility for firefighters, who can then effectively address fire impacts on the property.
